scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4618: Office/Principle department PCs (192.168.3.0/24) report
they cannot reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- the external-facing lab
segment has been unreachable all morning. The Office team believes the WAN/uplink
between the routers that carries traffic toward 128.168.0.0/16 went down. Please
find and confirm the fault, and tell us which link or device to bring back up.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The inter-router links are up, RIP is converged,
  and the 128.168.0.0/16 (Internet Lab) prefix is reachable from the Office segment;
  Office hosts reach 128.168.0.x with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a downed WAN/uplink that is not actually down.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Office (192.168.3.x) cannot
reach the Internet Lab (128.168.0.x) -- is NOT reproducible: an Office host reaches
128.168.0.x with 0% loss, the inter-router links carrying traffic toward
128.168.0.0/16 are up, ripd is running on router0/router1/router2, and the
128.168.0.0/16 prefix is present in the RIP tables.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the path to the Internet Lab is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the Office ->
Internet Lab path, finds it working, verifies the inter-router link state and the
128.168.0.0/16 route, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a downed WAN/uplink
to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — that Office/Principle department PCs (192.168.3.0/24 on
router1's eth0, and 192.168.4.0/24 on router1's eth1) cannot reach the Internet
Lab segment (128.168.0.0/16 on router2's eth1) — does not exist in the live lab.
End-to-end pings from both office_pc (192.168.3.2) and laptop0/pc0 (192.168.4.x)
to pc2 (128.168.0.2) complete with 0% packet loss. The WAN link between router1
and router2 (wan_r1_r2: 20.20.0.1 ↔ 20.20.0.2) is fully operational in both
directions. RIPv2 is running correctly on all routers: router1 has the
128.168.0.0/16 route installed via router2 (metric 2, eth3), and router2 has
return routes for both 192.168.3.0/24 and 192.168.4.0/24 via router1 (metric 2,
eth2). Both routers report zero bad packets and zero bad routes from all RIP
neighbors, and update timers are firing normally. All physical interfaces across
router0, router1, and router2 are in UP/UP state with the correct IP addresses.
There is no evidence of any WAN failure, RIP misconfiguration, missing route, or
reachability gap. The helpdesk ticket describes a fault that is not present —
the network is healthy and no corrective action is needed.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes the inter-router links are up and the 128.168.0.0/16 Internet Lab prefix is reachable from the Office segment at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states inter-router/WAN links and all interfaces are UP and shows successful end-to-end pings from Office hosts to 128.168.0.2 (0% loss) and the 128.168.0.0/16 route present, fulfilling the axis.

The agent's investigation produced direct observations (successful pings end-to-end and between routers, RIP status output, and running configs) that support the negative-fault conclusion; the writeup's claims follow logically from those observations though a few specific route/interface details are only implied by truncated outputs. Overall the evidence justifies 'no fault'.
